questions.knowledge_point: Dividing a Real Number by a Complex Number
questions.worked_solution:
The denominator is $5-3\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $5+3\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $5+3\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5-3\text{i}} & =\frac{2}{5-3\text{i}}\cdot \frac{5+3\text{i}}{5+3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{10+6\text{i}}{25+15\text{i}-15\text{i}-9{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{10+6\text{i}}{25-9{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{10+6\text{i}}{25-(9)(-1)} \\  & =\frac{10+6\text{i}}{25+9} \\  & =\frac{10+6\text{i}}{34}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{10+6\text{i}}{34}=\frac{10}{34}+\frac{6}{34}\text{i}=\frac{5}{17}+\frac{3}{17}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Dividing a Complex Number by an Imaginary Number
questions.problem: If ${z}_{1}=5-2\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=3\text{i}$, then ${z}_{1}$ divided by ${z}_{2}$ equals
questions.worked_solution:
First, we set up the fraction:

$$
\frac{5-2\text{i}}{3\text{i}}
$$

The denominator is the imaginary number $3\text{i}.$ Note that this can be written as $0+3\text{i},$ so the conjugate is $0-3\text{i},$ or simply $-3\text{i}.$

So, we multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-3\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{{z}_{1}}{{z}_{2}} & =\frac{5-2\text{i}}{3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{5-2\text{i}}{3\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-3\text{i}}{-3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-15\text{i}+6{\text{i}}^{2}}{-9{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-15\text{i}+6(-1)}{-9(-1)} \\  & =\frac{-6-15\text{i}}{9}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-6-15\text{i}}{9}=-\frac{6}{9}-\frac{15}{9}\text{i}=-\frac{2}{3}-\frac{5}{3}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Dividing an Imaginary Number by a Complex Number
questions.worked_solution:
The denominator is $1+3\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $1-3\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $1-3\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5\text{i}}{1+3\text{i}} & =\frac{5\text{i}}{1+3\text{i}}\cdot \frac{1-3\text{i}}{1-3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{5\text{i}-15{\text{i}}^{2}}{{1}^{2}-(3\text{i})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{5\text{i}-15(-1)}{1-(-9)} \\  & =\frac{5\text{i}+15}{10} \\  & =\frac{15+5\text{i}}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\frac{15+5\text{i}}{10}=(\frac{3}{2})+(\frac{1}{2})\,\text{i}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Dividing a Real Number by a Complex Number
questions.worked_solution:
The denominator is $3+4\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $3-4\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $3-4\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{3+4\text{i}} & =\frac{8}{3+4\text{i}}\cdot \frac{3-4\text{i}}{3-4\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{8(3-4\text{i})}{{3}^{2}-(4\text{i})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{24-32\text{i}}{9-(-16)} \\  & =\frac{24-32\text{i}}{25}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\frac{24-32\text{i}}{25}=(\frac{24}{25})+(-\frac{32}{25})\,\text{i}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Dividing a Real Number by a Complex Number
questions.worked_solution:
The denominator is $-2-3\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $-2+3\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-2+3\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{-2-3\text{i}} & =\frac{4}{-2-3\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-2+3\text{i}}{-2+3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{4(-2+3\text{i})}{(-2)^{2}-(3\text{i})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-8+12\text{i}}{4-(-9)} \\  & =\frac{-8+12\text{i}}{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\frac{-8+12\text{i}}{13}=(-\frac{8}{13})+(\frac{12}{13})\,\text{i}
$$
